key_idea: The centre of mass is lowest exactly when it coincides with the water surface, which gives a quadratic in the fill height.
sketch: With fill height x the centre of mass is c(x) = (dw*x^2/2 + da*(h^2-x^2)/2) / (dw*x + da*(h-x)); the radius cancels. Setting c'(x)=0 is equivalent to c(x)=x, i.e. (dw-da)/2*x^2 + da*h*x - da*h^2/2 = 0, whose positive root is x = h*(sqrt(da*dw)-da)/(dw-da). O(1); a ternary search on the unimodal c(x) works equally well. Pitfall: forgetting the air has mass (da>0), and r is a red herring.
